label: Kimi K3.1 Pro
output:
### ★★★★☆ Enough time to close a trade, but definitely not perfect

I bought the Kestrel Bastion 1500 on Voltwise for $229 in August 2026. It’s a 1500VA/1000W pure sine wave UPS, and I’m using it for my crypto trading setup in Miami: PC, three monitors, modem, and router.

The October 14 storm is why I’m writing this review. The power dropped around 2:20 p.m. while I was in a 10x long on a SOL perp. Not exactly the moment you want to watch your screens go black. The Bastion kept my rig and network equipment running, my internet stayed connected during that outage, and I was able to close the position cleanly in about four minutes. I didn’t try to keep trading until the battery died—I got out and started shutting everything down. For that alone, I’m glad I bought it.

I also tested the runtime on purpose instead of just trusting the box. My normal load while trading is around **410W according to the UPS’s own display**. The box claims approximately 14 minutes at 500W; at my actual load, I got **11 minutes 40 seconds before I chose to shut everything down**. That wasn’t running it completely flat, so your results will depend on your equipment, load, and when you decide to power off. Still, it gave me a realistic window to react. This is an emergency bridge, not something that’s going to run a full trading station for hours.

Pay attention to the outlets: there are **10 total, but only five are battery-backed**. The other five are surge-only. There’s also a 60W USB-C port. My biggest practical advice is to put your modem **and** router on the battery side. People protect their PC, forget the networking gear, and then lose their connection anyway. Also, don’t confuse the 1500VA rating with watts—the actual output rating is 1000W.

Now for the annoying stuff. During the first week, the fan randomly kicked on at 3 a.m. and woke me up. It’s loud, roughly like a hair dryer on low. The outage beeping is also extremely loud. You can mute it through the desktop app, but that setting reset after a firmware update, which was a fun surprise.

Speaking of the app, it looks like something from Windows XP. It’s ugly and feels dated, but the automatic shutdown function works, which matters more to me than a pretty interface. The unit also weighs around 30 pounds, so it’s not something you’ll want to keep moving around. The battery is swappable, at least, though the replacement pack costs $95.

So, four stars. It did the one thing I actually needed it to do and gave me enough time to manage a leveraged position instead of getting cut off mid-trade. The runtime was useful for my setup, and $229 felt reasonable for that peace of mind. I’m knocking off a star for the fan noise, loud alarm, reset settings, and outdated software. If you need minutes to exit trades and shut down safely, I’d recommend it. If you expect silent operation or extended runtime, look elsewhere or budget for something bigger.
